texts.label: text
texts.orig: Time brings renewed brilliance. In 2025, the global landscape experienced profound adjustments, geopolitical realignments, accelerating technological revolutions, escalating climate risks, and rapid transformation amid multiple changes in regulation, payment, and innovation competition across the pharmaceutical industry. The United Nations 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development has also entered a critical phase of overcoming challenges and breaking through bottlenecks. Against this evolving backdrop, the Group takes 'high-quality sustainable development' as its core, and deeply embeds ESG principles into its corporate strategy and operations. Guided by a long-term perspective, the Group actively fulfills its responsibilities as a corporate citizen, maintains strategic resolve amid uncertainty, and demonstrates its commitments through concrete actions.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: We advance to realize 'health for all' . Driven by the dual engines of 'product strength and commercialization,' we deepen the global collaborative R&D network and strengthen the in-house R&D system, continuously increasing R&D expenditure in advanced therapies, rare diseases, and areas of unmet medical need, promoting faster translation of innovative achievements into clinically accessible treatment practices. At the same time, upholding the principle of inclusive benefit, we actively promote equitable access to medical resources through initiatives such as reasonable pricing practices, drug assistance programs, and public health education. These efforts are designed to overcome geographic and economic barriers, strengthen healthcare delivery capacity in less-developed regions, and meaningfully fulfill our responsibilities in advancing public health. We also give back to society and jointly build resilient communities through public welfare actions, and promote social inclusion and common development through projects such as disaster relief, rural revitalization, care for vulnerable groups, and investment in education.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Guided by high standards of corporate governance, operational management, and business ethics, CMS embeds compliant operations and risk management and control into key processes including R&D, manufacturing, sales, human resources, finance, supply chain, and information security, improves forward-looking risk identification, early warning, and emergency response coordination mechanisms, strictly safeguards the bottom lines of integrity, anti-fraud, and data compliance, and continuously enhances transparency and accountability. We leverage digitalization and AI to drive process online enablement and lean management, improve operational efficiency and decision-making quality, and strengthen organizational resilience. We continue to strengthen our talent development framework and organizational support systems, strengthen competency and pipeline building for key positions, advance training empowerment and occupational health and safety management, and foster a workplace culture that inspires creativity, respects diversity, and cares for well-being, sharing development achievements with employees. At the same time, we have built a synergistic mechanism spanning the entire value chain, from innovation incubation to commercialization, while enforcing rigorous quality and safety controls at every stage and systematically managing environmental and social risks across our supply chain. In close partnership with industry stakeholders, we actively promote the development of a responsible, transparent, and resilient collaborative ecosystem, continuously creating shared value.

texts.orig: CMS (stock code: 0867.HK, 8A8.SG) is a platform company linking pharmaceutical innovation and commercialization with strong product lifecycle management capability, dedicated to providing competitive products and services to meet unmet healthcare needs.
texts.text: CMS (stock code: 0867.HK, 8A8.SG) is a platform company linking pharmaceutical innovation and commercialization with strong product lifecycle management capability, dedicated to providing competitive products and services to meet unmet healthcare needs.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The Group focuses on unmet clinical needs and drives innovation through a dual approach of 'collaborative R&D and inhouse R&D' . We build an innovative pipeline centered on first-in-class (FIC) and best-in-class (BIC) products, delivering more breakthrough disease solutions for patients. As of 16 March, 2026, the Group' s differentiated innovative pipeline has expanded to approximately 50 products, with a total of 7 innovative drugs and 2 orphan drugs approved for marketing in China to address unmet medical needs, of which 4 innovative drugs and 2 orphan drugs have been included in China' s National Reimbursement Drug List and achieved large-scale clinical application, thus enhancing the affordability and accessibility of the innovative products and safeguarding the lives and health of more patients.

texts.orig: Focusing on such fields of specialty diseases as Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic(CKM), central nervous system, gastroenterology, ophthalmology, and skin health business, the Group has adhered to responsible business operations with high ethical standards. It has built a differentiated product portfolio with academic value and high-quality standards. Through its influential academic platform and network, the Group provides professional products and services that empower the continuous translation of scientific research into clinical diagnosis and treatment practices. The Group is also actively advancing the 'industrial internationalization' strategy, leveraging Singapore as a hub for emerging markets to build an efficient, end-to-end value chain with strong 'R&D - manufacturing - commercialization' synergies. Following our secondary listing in Singapore, we have further strengthened strategic recognition and connectivity to resources in international market, enabling new avenues for high-quality, sustainable growth.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: As the highest leadership and decision-making body for ESG-related matters, the Board of Directors of the Company places great importance on sustainable development, continuously strengthens the ESG governance framework, and promotes the integration of its own operations, ESG strategy, and social and environmental harmony, with the objective of creating long-term sustainable value for stakeholders.
texts.text: As the highest leadership and decision-making body for ESG-related matters, the Board of Directors of the Company places great importance on sustainable development, continuously strengthens the ESG governance framework, and promotes the integration of its own operations, ESG strategy, and social and environmental harmony, with the objective of creating long-term sustainable value for stakeholders.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The Company has formed a three-tier ESG governance framework consisting of the Board of Directors, the ESG Committee and the ESG Working Group. The Board of Directors of the Company is the highestlevel supervisory body for ESG strategy, management and execution, and is responsible for overall supervision, direction and review. The ESG Committee is chaired by the executive director of the Company, who leads the ESG management work, and three independent non-executive directors are appointed as committee members, among which Ms. Luo Ying was appointed as a member of the ESG Committee on March 16, 2026. The organization-wide ESG Working Group is responsible for comprehensively promoting and implementing ESG-related work.

During the Reporting Period, the Board of Directors convened four ESG Committee meetings to oversee and review the latest progress in healthcare accessibility, business ethics, product quality, employee training and development, ESG targets, and corresponding work plans.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: To further integrate ESG governance with the incentive system, the Group has formally established the CMS Non-financial Key Performance Indicators and Management Remuneration Linkage Mechanism . The mechanism incorporates key ESG indicators such as business ethics, product quality and safety, and climate change into the performance evaluation system for executive directors, senior management, and relevant management personnel, explicitly linking ESG indicators to 10% of the yearend bonus. This initiative aims to extend ESG targets from the strategic level of the Board of Directors to the front line of business implementation, promoting the management to comprehensively fulfill sustainability responsibilities while pursuing business performance. By directly linking ESG performance to remuneration incentives, the Group not only strengthens the execution of ESG initiatives, but also helps achieve an organic balance between long-term sustainable value and short-term operational performance, providing an institutional safeguard for its high-quality and responsible development.

texts.orig: ·	Ursofalk (Ursodeoxycholic Acid Oral Suspension) was approved for marketing in China in July 2024 and was included in the Category B of NRDL in December 2025. Among its approved indications, one is a rare disease (for the treatment of liver disease associated with a condition called cystic fibrosis in children aged 1 month to 18 years), making it the first approved drug for this indication in China. Moreover, the product is an oral suspension that further meets clinical medication needs of patients with rare diseases and pediatric diseases due to its unique new variety, dosage form and specification as a pediatric drug, which is in line with the physiological characteristics of children.

texts.orig: In addition, PharmaGend, an associate company of the Group based in Singapore, has gradually developed into an international one-stop pharmaceutical CDMO platform with high-standard drug manufacturing capabilities, empowering global pharmaceutical companies to rapidly enter emerging markets. The annual capacity of its oral solid dosage (OSD) has reached 1.5 billion units, while capacity expansion for the construction of new production lines for nasal sprays, creams, and injectables, as well as a packaging center, is progressing smoothly. These efforts are expected to improve local drug manufacturing and supply capabilities and, to some extent, contribute to the advancement of the regional pharmaceutical industrialization level. Meanwhile, Rxilient and PharmaGend have actively collaborated to jointly advance the localization technology transfer of key products, with a view to achieving localized production as soon as possible and improving access to Global high-quality products in emerging markets. In addition, Rxilient also allows local distributors to supply products directly to the Southeast Asian market, enhancing the timeliness of drug distribution in developing countries and benefiting more patients.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The Group attaches great importance to risk management and internal controls and has established a risk management structure with clear roles and responsibilities. The Board of Directors is the highest decision-making body for the Company' s comprehensive risk management. Each year, the Group reports the annual audit work plan, audit findings, risk warnings, improvement measures, and progress updates to the Company' s Board of Directors. The Audit Committee under the Company' s Board of Directors is responsible for reviewing the work plans and results of internal and external audits, in order to ensure sufficient assistance to the Board in supervising and reviewing the effectiveness of the Group' s risk management and internal control system and to timely identify significant risks that may affect the Group' s operations.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The Group continuously optimizes its risk management system, policies, and work procedures to comprehensively identify and control potential risks. According to internal actual needs, internal audit work is carried out, and the Group' s audit plan covers all operating entities and major business segments at least annually. During the Reporting Period, the Group conducted 11 internal audits, covering areas such as expenses, procurement, and compliance risk inspections. During the audit process, the Group applied data analysis to identify potential risks at key control points and propose optimization suggestions. All audit results are based on the  CMS Internal Audit Policy , forming special reports submitted for management review. The corrective actions and rectification progress of the audited units are dynamically tracked, creating an 'audit-feedback-improvement' closed-loop management process to continuously enhance the level of risk prevention and control.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The Group strictly adheres to the ethical guidelines for clinical trials, following the ethical principles of the Declaration of Helsinki and relevant regulatory requirements, consistently prioritizing the protection of the rights and interests of trial subjects. All human clinical trials of the Group are conducted after obtaining approvals from the drug administration authorities and having passed ethical reviews. Before participating in a clinical trial, all subjects are required to sign the  Informed Consent Form of Subjects, which clearly stipulates that they shall have the right to be informed and the freedom to choose, and that they have the right to refuse or withdraw from the clinical trial at any time, thereby protecting their rights and interests.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: In terms of source control, the Group has established a strict material selection mechanism. The Group dynamically updates the list of qualified suppliers through implementing hierarchical management, on-site audits, and annual performance reviews of suppliers. For key material suppliers who have significant impacts on drug quality and medication safety, the Group arranges on-site inspections and quality audits on a yearly basis, prioritizing the materials provided by qualified suppliers with high comprehensive scores to ensure the quality of raw materials from the source. In addition, for all incoming materials, the Group conducts strict incoming inspection by checking the appearance of materials and verifying material-related information, etc. The Group also conducts sampling inspection according to the Sampling Management Procedures,  and releases the materials for production after they are accepted as qualified, with a traceable material information database to refine the material control process.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: During the quality admission and acceptance process, the Group strictly inspects finished products in accordance with national product standards or product quality standards approved by the National Medical Products Administration (NMPA). For imported drug products, the Group strictly follows the requirements of national laws and regulations and undergoes stringent inspections by the Institute for Food and Drug Control, including the first batch of imported drugs, biological products, products after standard change or manufacturing process alteration, etc., and may require issuing the Import Inspection Report as necessary. Upon the arrival of the imported and domestic drug products, the Quality Management Department of the corresponding subsidiaries in drug operation business of the Group will conduct batch-by-batch inspections as per GSP requirements, and verify the product inspection reports. In case of any product quality issues, the Group will handle the problematic products by isolating, reporting, returning, or destroying them in accordance with the Operating Procedures for Reporting and Confirming Unqualified Drugs  and the Operating Procedures for Destruction of Unqualified Drugs , ensuring that unqualified products never enter the market. In addition, the Group has established an independent special drug safety management system to implement stricter compliance management controls for specific products.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The Group' s Registration Management Department is responsible for leading the drafting and revision of package inserts and labels. In the event of updates of relevant laws and regulations, approval of drug marketing applications, re-registration and other changes related to package inserts and labels, the Registration Management Department of the Group will evaluate the type of change based on the relevant laws and regulations and initiate the corresponding drafting or revision process accordingly. For changes that require reporting, the Registration Management Department will organize an internal review and submit a supplementary application or filing to the regulatory authorities in accordance with procedures. If any such change only requires submission in the annual report, it will be included in the drug annual report as stipulated. After review, approval and release by the department head and relevant partners,  the revised package inserts and labels will be officially put into use.

In addition to routine duty performance, the Committees hold regular meetings annually to comprehensively review the annual pharmacovigilance work report and the effectiveness of risk control measures. This ensures that the drug safety management system continuously complies with regulatory requirements and business development needs, enabling the Group to effectively fulfill its primary responsibility for drug safety.

In addition, for commercialized products, the Group prepares the  Periodic Drug Safety Update Report  and the  Pharmacovigilance Plan  for each drug to continuously analyze and proactively prevent potential risks, thereby achieving a closed-loop management process from monitoring, assessment to intervention.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: During the preliminary supplier review stage, the Group also collects the  Manufacturer Questionnaire for more efficient communications and decision-making. texts.label: text
texts.orig: The Group implements hierarchical management for qualified suppliers according to the impact of their materials on product quality and safety. According to the Provisions for Material Supplier Management  and the relationship between materials and key product quality, suppliers are classified into Grade I (primary/non-primary) suppliers and Grade II suppliers. Among them, Grade I suppliers provide materials that directly affect the key quality of products (such as raw and auxiliary materials, and packaging materials in direct contact with products), while Grade II suppliers provide materials that indirectly affect quality (such as external packaging materials, and testing reagents).

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Based on the assessment scores, a comprehensive supplier score is formed to achieve differentiated risk management. Suppliers with a comprehensive material supplier evaluation score of 70 or above, who have completed the rectification of deficiencies identified during the assessment process, may be considered as qualified suppliers for the Company once their rectification documentation or plans are submitted and verified. The higher the comprehensive evaluation score, the longer the supplier assessment cycle may be appropriately extended.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: If a supplier is found to be unqualified during a quality re-inspection, the Group will issue a nonconformity report and inform the supplier in time to return of the unqualified goods. Suppliers who fail to meet the Group's requirements twice in a year will be disqualified. If goods are found with any severe defect or significant quality risks, the Group will suspend procurement from this supplier to prevent and reduce quality risks. In addition, for suppliers with a comprehensive score below 70 points, and who still do not meet the requirements after reassessment following rectification, the Group will also terminate cooperation with them. During the Reporting Period, the Group terminated cooperation with  3 suppliers.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The Group strictly implements supplier quality management. The Supply Chain Management Department of the Group and relevant departments jointly implement strict inspection on qualification report and receipt for imported and domestic finished products to ensure that the products meet the national quality standards. Once any quality problem is found, the Group will immediately gain an in-depth understanding of the causes, provide feedback to the suppliers, urge them to rectify and provide necessary supports. If a supplier fails a sampling inspection conducted by an institute for drug control or has any major quality issues, is subject to a recall order, or has a poor quality reputation, etc., the Group' s Quality Management Department will organize on-site visits, make an all-round risk assessment, and focus on the supplier' s quality management system and the effectiveness of the supplier' s corrective measures. For suppliers assessed as unqualified, the Group will terminate the cooperation with them in accordance with the supplier exit mechanism to ensure the product quality.

texts.orig: To continuously identify and manage ESG risks in the supply chain, the Group systematically conducted an ESG questionnaire survey for suppliers during the Reporting Period. The survey content covered multiple dimensions, including business ethics, product and service quality assurance, human rights protection, occupational health and safety, and environmental protection, aiming to assess suppliers' actual conditions in ESG policy formulation, management measure implementation, and risk control. This work helps the Group to more comprehensively grasp the ESG performance of the supply chain and provides a basis for subsequent risk management and collaborative improvement.

texts.orig: The Group is committed to promoting integrity and transparency in supply chain management, integrating principles of integrity and compliance into procurement practices. Through a combination of institutional constraints, capacity building, and continuous supervision, the Group systematically builds an ecosystem of honest and transparent business cooperation. The Group explicitly incorporates antibribery and anti-corruption clauses in all supplier agreements and requires them to strictly comply with the laws and regulations of their operating locations. At the same time, through signing the  Supplier Initiative Letter , the Group promotes partners' joint commitment to adhere to regulations regarding business ethics, human rights guidelines, environmental protection, and respect for community culture, etc.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: To continuously enhance suppliers' compliance awareness, the Group has also established a regular integrity management mechanism: Continuously collecting suppliers' internal anti-corruption policies and regulations to ensure that suppliers have a comprehensive anti-corruption management system, and actively communicating with each supplier regarding the latest anti-corruption requirements and trends in their respective industries. Each subsidiary of the Group conducts annual compliance training for suppliers and distributors through an online platform. In addition, we incorporate the integrity performance of suppliers into the scope of on-site audits, focusing on examining their implementation of relevant regulations and the fulfillment of relevant initiatives, to ensure that integrity responsibilities effectively extend to all aspects of the supply chain.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The Group has established a transparent anti-corruption whistleblowing and feedback mechanism for upstream and downstream partners. Partners can provide feedback via email, telephone contact, official website, face-to-face communication, etc. In the course of cooperation with the Group, partners may conduct whistleblowing either anonymously or with their real names through the aforesaid channels if they find that any employee is involved in irregular behaviors such as bribery and corruption, unfair competition, disclosure of commercial or technical secrets, and abuse of authority. Upon receipt of a whistleblowing submission, the Group' s Supply Management Department will collaborate with the Compliance Department and other relevant units to immediately initiate risk identification, assessment, and investigation procedures within the compliance framework. Special inspections will be conducted as necessary to ensure that all whistleblowing submissions are handled promptly and fairly, thus jointly maintaining a clean and regulated business ecosystem.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The Group has a zero-tolerance stance toward child labor and forced labor, conducts background checks before recruitment, and requires the Human Resources Center to ensure the authenticity and validity of the candidates' identity are verified during the recruitment process through inquiry, verification of identity documents and obtaining signed confirmation from candidates. The Group also encourages employees to report illegal employment cases to superiors in charge for timely investigation and follow-up actions. If any violation, such as child labor or forced labor, is found, employment will be identified as invalid, the employment contract will be immediately terminated, and the salary, benefits and other remuneration prescribed by law will be paid. Meanwhile, the Group has correspondingly established an accountability mechanism, in which relevant personnel responsible will be punished according to the severity of the circumstances to prevent a recurrence of such events. During the Reporting Period, the Group employed no child labor or forced labor.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The Group provides employees with fair and reasonable remuneration and benefits, ensuring that employee remuneration is not lower than the national and local minimum wage standards. It is committed to paying employees' wages in full and on time, and clearly lists the lawful deductions on pay slips to ensure transparency and fairness in remuneration payments. At the same time, the Group upholds the principle of equal pay for equal work, ensuring that male and female employees receive equal remuneration and all employees get fair and reasonable remuneration for their roles.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The Group strictly complies with labor-related laws and regulations and firmly prohibits any form of forced labor. The Group implements standard statutory working hours, on that basis, offers flexible work arrangements into practice to enable employees to reasonably schedule work and leisure time according to responsibilities and department demands, thereby facilitating a better work-life balance. In the context of overtime culture not being advocated, employees who need to work overtime due to work arrangements should submit overtime requests to department heads for evaluation and approval. Upon completion of overtime work, the employees will be provided with compensatory leave or overtime pay for work performed on national statutory holidays according to regulations.

texts.label: text

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The Group deeply integrates environmental protection into its business operations by systematically managing GHG, waste, and the use of resources. It practices responsible operations and production responsibilities, driving synergistic development between its business and the ecosystem. The Group' s business with direct impacts on the environment mainly includes pharmaceutical sales and marketing business, pharmaceutical production business and agriculture and livestock business 4 . The Group' s pharmaceutical production business is relatively small in scale. During the Reporting Period, the sales of self-produced products only accounted for around 0.7% of the Group' s revenue under the assumption that all revenue was generated from pharmaceutical product sales. Due to the Group' s business distribution characteristics, the total emission of GHG and environmental pollutants was limited, and the impact on the ecological environment was insignificant.

Based on compliance with environmental protection-related laws and regulations in the places of operation, the Group continuously monitors policy developments, has publicly issued the CMS Environmental Protection, Occupational Health and Safety (EHS) Management Policy , and has set environmental management targets with respect to GHG emissions, waste, energy consumption, and water resource usage, striving to enhance its capabilities in addressing climate change and environmental protection. texts.label: text
texts.orig: To systematically control and optimize corporate environmental practices, the Group has established an environmental governance system encompassing the Board of Directors, the ESG Committee under the Board, and the ESG Working Group. The Board of Directors of the Company is the highest-level governance body for environmental management strategy and performance. The ESG Committee under the Board is responsible for overseeing the management guidelines, policies and structures of environmental protection, overall supervising and managing ESG-related risks and opportunities, and collaborating with the Audit Department and the ESG Working Group to identify and address these risks. The ESG Working Group is primarily responsible for implementation, including the formulation of specific environmental management plans, the collection, consolidation, and analysis of data on pollution emissions, energy use, and water consumption from all responsible entities. These activities support reporting to the ESG Committee and assist the Board in continuously monitoring the Group' s management of energy conservation and emission reduction, as well as the achievement of environmental targets. During the Reporting Period, the Board of Directors of the Company and the ESG Committee reviewed the Group' s environmental management strategy, the implementation of environmental management, and the progress of environmental targets.

texts.orig: The Audit Department conducts annual internal audits of all operational entities regarding environment and energy consumption, and compiles special audit reports for review by the ESG Committee. During the Reporting Period, the Group conducted a comprehensive on-site audit regarding the environment and energy consumption, covering the pharmaceutical production business, agriculture and livestock business, office areas, and all other operational entities. The status (such as environmental governance, environmental facilities, energy use, storage and disposal of hazardous waste, and employee safety) was comprehensively reviewed and problems of each audited entity were systematically identified, assessed, and explained in detail. Based on the audit results, the Audit Department provided recommendations to the relevant responsible entities for rectification, assisted them in formulating comprehensive improvement plans, regularly tracked the progress of corrective actions, and issued the Special Audit Report on ESG Environment and Energy Consumption.

To systematically address related challenges and opportunities, the Group has established a top-down climate change governance structure to ensure that climate issues are effectively integrated into corporate strategy, risk management, and daily operations. texts.label: text
texts.orig: Based on the climate-related disclosure framework, benchmarking against industry best practices, and drawing extensively on external expert opinions, the Group systematically identifies potential climate risks and opportunities that may arise in the short-term and mid-to-long-term business development stages, and ultimately establishes the CMS Climate-Related Risk and Opportunity Register. Concurrently, the Group deeply engages a professional third-party institution to apply appropriately selected climate scenarios and core parameters, and to prioritize its climate-related risks through qualitative and quantitative analyses based on its business characteristics and future development trends.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The Group carried out a systematic review of its business and assets around the world, and selected internationally authoritative and highly comparable scenario frameworks based on the differences in the nature of risks. In light of the continuous evolution of international climate-related disclosure standards and climate science research, to further enhance the alignment of climate risk analysis with the latest international best practices and improve the forward-looking and detailed level of analysis results, the Group optimized and updated the climate scenario settings during the Reporting Period. For physical risks, the Group adopts the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC)' s Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSP) scenarios, and for transition risks, it adopts the Network for Greening the Financial System (NGFS) scenarios. texts.orig: During the Reporting Period, by referring to the Water Risk Filter, a global tool for assessing water risk developed by World Wide Fund for Nature (WWF), the Group updated the water resource risk assessment for the areas where all physical assets are located with the update of its physical asset portfolio. texts.label: text
texts.orig: To address water-related risks and reduce water consumption, all subsidiaries of the Group have developed water use monitoring and management mechanisms, and the Group' s manufacturing subsidiary conducts a routine inspection of purified water once a week and a systematic verification once a year in accordance with the methods specified in the  Pharmacopoeia of the People' s Republic of China ; according to the requirements of national standards, drinking water is inspected once a month, and a qualified third-party institution is commissioned for annual audit and inspection. Hunan Agriculture and Livestock, a subsidiary of the Group, formulated the  Hunan Agriculture and Livestock Water Testing Methods . Adopting the inspection methods of 'visual inspection, odor detection, observation, taste testing, and verification' , the tap water is inspected every month, and the health inspection and quarantine authorities conduct onsite centralized inspection and testing once a year, thereby ensuring that the water quality meets the standard and guaranteeing water safety.

texts.orig: The Group deeply recognizes that the normal operation of its business is closely intertwined with a healthy and well-functioning ecosystem, and therefore proactively takes preventive measures to minimize adverse impacts on the ecological environment and biodiversity. The Group strictly abides by the  Forest Law of the People' s Republic of China, the  Law of the People' s Republic of China on Wildlife Protection  and other relevant laws and regulations, and the United Nations'  Convention on Biological Diversity  and other international conventions, and has developed internal policies including the  CMS Environmental Protection, Occupational Health and Safety (EHS) Management Policy , providing institutional safeguards for biodiversity conservation.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The Group pledges to maintain zero deforestation in future operations and systematically manage the potential impacts of its business activities on the ecological environment and biodiversity. The Group prioritizes the use of environmentally friendly technologies and materials and, in planning new, renovation or expansion projects, intentionally avoids locations with important biodiversity and environmentally sensitive areas, and adopts technologies and measures with a lower environmental impact to avoid negative effects. If negative impacts occurred, the Group will take remedial measures in a timely manner.

texts.orig: The Group also systematically integrates biodiversity protection into value chain management. In the downstream supply chain stage, the Group actively advocates and encourages suppliers to promote biodiversity protection in their operations and business activities. Through coordinated, end-to-end value chain management, the Group is committed to fulfilling its responsibility for ecological sustainability while achieving business objectives.

texts.label: footnote
texts.orig: 14  The air pollutant statistics of the Group mainly covers the exhaust gas generated from its production operations. The annual emission of air pollutants is an estimated value, which is calculated from the total natural gas consumption of the boiler, the fixed gas consumption rate of the boiler, and the emission rate. The emission rate comes from the test report of a professional third party hired by the Group, so the emission rate is related to the production status and fuel quality at the test time point. During the Reporting Period, the increase in air pollutant emissions was primarily attributable to higher production volumes driven by business demand.

texts.label: footnote
texts.orig: 17  The indirect GHG emissions (Scope 2) mainly arise from indirect emissions due to the consumption of externally purchased electricity during the Group's operations and production processes. In 2025, 2024 and 2023, GHG emissions in Hong Kong were calculated with reference to the emission factors disclosed in HK Electric's Sustainability Report for 2024, 2023 and 2022, respectively. For Macau, the emission factors applied in 2023 and 2024 were the operating-region emission factors; in 2025, GHG emissions in Macau were calculated with reference to the emission factors disclosed in Companhia de Electricidade de Macau (CEM)'s 2024 Sustainability Report. For operating locations outside Hong Kong and Macau, the relevant emission factors of the countries/regions were used. In particular, for 2025, the electricity emission factor for Mainland China adopted the grid emission factor of 0.5306 tCO2/MWh as specified in the Announcement on the release of the 2023 Electricity Carbon Dioxide Emission Factors, issued by the  the Ministry of Ecology and Environment on 31 December 2025.

texts.orig: 18  During the Reporting Period, the indirect GHG emissions (Scope 3) changed compared to last year, mainly due to two factors: 1)  in 2025, Scope 3 emissions under 'Upstream Transportation and Distribution' decreased mainly due to optimization of transportation modes and routes; this category captures only emissions from orders for which the Group is responsible for arranging transportation under the agreed trade terms with upstream suppliers (rather than all orders); This category specifically accounts for emissions arising from orders where transportation is arranged by the Group according to predefined trade agreements with upstream manufacturers, rather than encompassing all orders placed by the Group; 2) the sample of the employee commuting questionnaire changes in the composition (e.g., an increase in the number of employees who commute long distances and by private vehicles) and an increase in the number of employees have led to an increase in GHG emissions(Scope 3) in the category of 'Employee Commuting'. Please refer to Appendix V for the detailed calculation method of GHG emissions(Scope 3).

table_cells.text: Unclear responsibilities or poor communication may lead to delays in addressing critical issues, impacting decision-making efficiency and external perceptions.
A sound governance system helps enhance transparency and trust, supporting long-term, stable development.

With the Board of Directors as the highest decision- making and supervisory body, the Company has established an internal governance structure with clearly defined responsibilities and authorities. It defines strategic vision and drives implementation through regular meetings, establishes stakeholder communication mechanisms, conducts issue assessments, and progressively integrates risks into the overall management system.
Inadequate risk control mechanisms or ineffective implementation of the 'three lines of defense' may lead to compliance incidents, corruption, or audit deficiencies, resulting in financial losses.
Enhancing risk management helps prevent operational risks, improve compliance capabilities, and boost corporate credibility.

With the Board of Directors as the highest decision- making body, the Company has established a well- defined organizational structure and reinforced the 'three lines of defense' framework, strengthening controls through internal and external audits and a closed-loop 'audit - feedback - improvement' process. Centered on business ethics, the Group has improved its anti-corruption policies, implemented full-coverage employee training, and established multi-department monitoring mechanisms, integrating risk management into the overall risk control system.
Bribery, fraud, and other violations may lead to regulatory penalties, termination of cooperation, and reputational crises, directly affecting operational stability.
Strict adherence to ethical standards helps reduce improper expenditures, solidify cooperative relationships, and enhance recognition in the capital market.

The Group has established a four-dimensional control system comprising a policy framework, multi-level supervisory organizations, comprehensive training and communication, and routine monitoring and assessment. Through policy updates, training and evaluations, internal and external audits, and accountability measures, the Group comprehensively mitigates related risks.
Insufficient talent reserves, lack of competitive remuneration, or limited career development opportunities may lead to vacancies in key positions, affecting business advancement.
Establishing systematic mechanisms helps attract and retain core talent, stimulating organizational vitality.

The Group regards talent as a core driver and has established a human resources management framework. It attracts talent through compliant employment practices, diversified recruitment, talent reviews, and team construction; retains talent by providing fair incentives, competitive remuneration and benefits, employee care, and clear promotion pathways; safeguards human rights, and conducts regular internal and external audits.
A disconnect between training and strategy or uneven resource allocation may lead to capability gaps, affecting business implementation and talent team construction.
Improving the training system helps enhance professional and leadership skills, achieving mutual growth between individuals and the Company.

Focusing on strategy and employee needs, the Group has established a training system that builds a diverse framework of 'online + offline' and 'internal + external' courses, covering occupational skills, professional skills, leadership, and general force. Through needs assessment, resource optimization, and digital empowerment, combined with a promotion mechanism, the Group ensures the effective implementation of training.
Supplier disqualification, unstable quality, or logistics disruptions may lead to product safety issues or production halts.
Establishing an efficient supply chain system helps ensure supply stability, control costs, and enhance operational resilience.

The Group has constructed an end-to-end management system, and builds a resilient and sustainable supply chain leveraging dedicated policies, tiered supplier assessments, differentiated risk control and mitigation measures, together with risk management, integrity and compliance initiatives, and supplier training.

table_cells.text: Unreasonable pricing, insufficient supply at the grassroots level, or slow implementation of innovative drugs may lead to increased patient burden, affecting social image.
Enhancing accessibility helps expand market coverage, increase public recognition, and explore emerging market opportunities.

The Company has established a governance and control system centered on the Board of Directors and enhances medical accessibility and affordability comprehensively through fair pricing, promoting the inclusion of products in the NRDL, multi-level supply chain building, acceleration of innovative drug launches, expansion of emerging markets, nonprofit science education initiatives and drug donation activities, and the supportive training of healthcare professionals.
Infringement or mismanagement of intellectual property rights may lead to legal disputes, asset loss, and impact R&D progress and competitive advantage.
Strengthening end- to-end lifecycle management helps protect innovation outcomes and unlocks the commercial value of R&D.

The Group has established a specialized management system, a comprehensive process control system, a regular prevention and control mechanism, specialized training, and diverse monitoring and reporting channels for systematic intellectual property protection and risk management.
Failure to keep pace with clinical needs or guideline updates may lead to insufficient product recognition, affecting market promotion.
Deep participation in the development of guidelines and academic consensus helps enhance product credibility through authoritative validation and market competitiveness.

The Group has leveraged its role as a bridge within the pharmaceutical industry to support the inclusion of core products in authoritative domestic and international treatment guidelines and expert consensus. It has actively participated in academic exchanges and deepened industry- academia-research collaborations, contributing to high-quality industry development through clinical standardization, academic co- construction, and talent cultivation.
High R&D investment and long cycles may lead to unrecoverable costs if clinical trials fail or approvals are delayed, affecting long-term performance.
Continued investment in innovation and strategic focus on the fields of specialty and rare diseases helps enrich the product line and drive long- term growth.

Focusing on patient needs, the Group continuously increases investment through independent R&D, industrial investment, and strategic cooperation, establishes a end-to-end lifecycle R&D system, concentrates on advantageous areas, efficiently advances clinical development and commercialization, and simultaneously strengthens intellectual property protection.
Unstable material quality, production or storage lapses may lead to drug safety issues, resulting in recalls and reputational damage.
Establishing a full value chain quality system helps ensure drug safety and shapes a professional and reliable brand image.

The Group has established a comprehensive quality system covering the entire process of source control, production and operation, storage and transportation, traceability management, and complaint handling, ensuring the quality of products and services through internal and external audits, system optimization, personnel assessment, and closed-loop rectification.
False marketing content, non- compliant information, or inadequate cost control could lead to regulatory penalties and legal risks, damaging brand reputation.
Establishing a compliant marketing mechanism helps build a professional image and gain the trust of medical institutions and regulatory authorities.

The Group has established a closed-loop management mechanism of 'policy - implementation - monitoring - feedback'. Leveraging dedicated policies, end-to-end review of promotional materials, regular training for all employees, multi-level monitoring and assessment, and a whistleblower protection system, the Group comprehensively manages related risks.

table_cells.text: Respective business departments of investment, R&D, production, sales, and procurement
Establish clear and specific business objectives and plans; Set up rules and processes for business management; Implement execution and supervision relying on information systems.
A risk management system collaboratively operated by multiple departments, including the Legal Department, Compliance Department, Operation Management Department, and Finance and Accounting Center.

Legal Department: Responsible for the management and control of risks in external cooperation such as contract signing and product introduction; Compliance Department: Responsible for the improvement and supervision of the compliance system; Operation Management Department: Responsible for the supervision and control of the business activities of each operating unit; Finance and Accounting Center: Responsible for conducting overall control through management tools such as budgeting and fund management.
Focuses on the Group's key operations, conducts independent evaluations of the management at the Group headquarters and its subsidiaries, oversees the risk management of each operating entity.

table_cells.text: The Group has adopted measures such as internal document separation, document encryption, and data classification management, and has established an operating mechanism and rules for review, approval and authorization for access to customer information. Employees are required to strictly access, query and maintain personal and customer data with authorization, and unauthorized employees are not permitted to use, export or copy any customer information.

The Group regularly inspects the information system access, including but not limited to the authorization mechanism, process, user access, access scope confirmation for in- service employees, and access clearance for departing employees. During the Reporting Period, the Group conducted an annual information system access inspection for internal office system cloud platform to ensure the reasonableness of access settings and security of the relevant data.

The Group signs confidentiality agreements with employees, conveying and emphasizing the importance of confidentiality responsibilities and the legal consequences of breach. Employees are encouraged to prevent, stop, and report all related violations through channels such as telephone, email, and internal work software. For confidential data or personal information, sensitive information is desensitized.

For suppliers who may have access to private information of consumers, the Group strictly constrains supplier behavior through contractual agreements, to protect customers' rights related to privacy and personal information.

table_cells.text: Adverse reactions/events and other safety information are collected by a designated full-time employee of the Pharmacovigilance Department.

All employees shall report the relevant information to the Pharmacovigilance Department as per the principle of 'report immediately upon suspicion'; Reports obtained from other sources are handled in accordance with relevant processes and time limits.

The Pharmacovigilance Department is responsible for calling back, and assisting in follow-up investigation; If combined with quality complaints, submitting to the Quality Management Department for further handling according to relevant processes; Activating an emergency plan in the event of a major safety event;

Submitting reports to domestic and overseas regulatory authorities; Submitting the reports to domestic and overseas partners/drug marketing authorization holders as required by the safety data exchange protocol; Taking immediate and effective measures based on the procedure in case of a major safety event/major change in safety information; Regularly assessing and controlling the risks of the Group's products.

table_cells.text: • Adhering to the principle of openness,fairness and impartiality, preventing and controlling possible corruption risks in the bidding process with participation of multiple departments; • Including human rights, environmental and social factors into the annual supplier assessment and review; encouraging and inclined to choose suppliers advocating the green environmental protection concept or with relevant qualifications, including but not limited to: ISO 14000, ISO 45001, SA8000, AEO, Transported Asset Protection Association (TAPA), etc.; • Under similar objective conditions, prioritizing the supplier that is geographically closer and more easily accessible if the candidates are on a par, in order to reduce the potential environmental pollution during transportation.

• Clearly stating quality integrity, supply integrity, anti-corruption and other compliance requirements in agreements signed with suppliers, and requiring suppliers to comply with national and industry standards related to product operations and production; • Formulating the Provisions for Material Supplier Management , which clearly defines the scope of supplier audits, including dimensions such as legal operation, product quality, environment and governance; • Requiring suppliers to comply with environmental standards for packaging materials. The inner packaging in contact with drugs is required to be at least the food-grade packaging to realize green packaging.

• Conducting all-round assessment in terms of qualification and capacities, to ensure product quality during the distribution process and to minimize the potential impact of goods circulation on the surrounding environment; • Including environmental and social factors in selection criteria for logistics service providers and distributors, including enterprise qualification, warehousing and distribution capacities, staffing, operational management, channel coverage, response efficiency, reputation in the industry and dedication to environmental protection; • Prioritizing distributors with TAPA certification, complying with GSP requirements, larger scale in the sales region, comprehensive distribution channels coverage and dedication to social responsibility and environmental protection; • Making a series of internal management regulations available to logistics service providers and distributors, to ensure that partners are aware of and comply with the Group's requirements and standards for product quality and safety, anti-corruption, intellectual property protection, data privacy protection, compliant employment, and environmental protection; • Adding relevant terms related to anti-corruption, anti-bribery and compliance operation to the cooperation contracts signed with logistics service providers and distributors, requiring logistics service providers and distributors to confirm their compliance with the Group's relevant provisions; • Conducting audits related to the Good Distribution Practice (GDP) for logistics service providers and regularly assessing and improving their operational quality; • Monitoring logistics service providers' environmental management practices and carbon emissions during the logistics processes, and sharing current measures available to control the increase in carbon emissions; • Providing training to international logistics service providers on related topics such as product transportation quality and environmental protection.

table_cells.text: • The Group regards campus recruitment as a key source of its talent pipeline, and vigorously carries out programs for interns and management trainees. • During the Reporting Period, the Group held about 66 online and in person campus recruitment seminars and 73 campus job fairs, and issued offers to 1,338 excellent graduates.

• In addition to traditional social recruitment channels, such as professional human resource websites and headhunting firms, the Group has established official recruitment accounts on multiple social media and platforms to post the latest recruitment information, which helps attract potential candidates more effectively and assists job seekers in obtaining recruitment information conveniently through diverse channels. • The Group has also developed mechanisms and incentive policies for recommending excellent talents, which motivate all employees and the public to actively recommend talents. • During the Reporting Period, the Group successfully recruited 722 professionals through experienced hiring channels.

• The Group encourages internal transfers and competitive recruitment to broaden the candidate pool for core positions and provide employees with new career development opportunities. • During the Reporting Period, the Group posted 7 internal recruitment notices, and 436 employees completed internal transfers.

table_cells.text: Risk type: Policy and legal risk
• Increasing pressures from GHG emission reduction policies; • The price of GHG emission rights increases; • Litigation over climate or environmental issues may occur.

Impact on business model • Countries/regions around the world are promoting GHG emission reduction by formulating and implementing global emission reduction targets and policies, companies are in an external environment where emission reduction compliance requirements are continuously tightening, and business decisions need to fully consider the potential impacts brought by policy constraints; • In order to achieve the 2℃ target of the Paris Agreement , governments domestically and abroad are gradually improving carbon pricing policies, mainly through carbon trading mechanisms and carbon tax systems, and companies are facing the pressure of higher pricing of GHG emission rights; • The intensity of regulatory enforcement in the environmental field is continuously escalating, and companies may face an increased frequency and number of environmental and climate-related lawsuits, with associated legal and reputational risks rising simultaneously. Impact on the value chain • Systematic assessments on the supply chain shall be implemented to ensure regulatory compliance.

table_cells.text: • Upon receipt of strong wind warnings, suspend outdoor elevated work, dust-generating construction, and large-scale outdoor activities; • Upon receipt of typhoon warnings, organize staff in advance for shelter and risk avoidance while suspending outdoor work; • Bring forward the execution of cooperation agreements with third-party warehouses. In case of typhoons or other extreme weather events, launch third-party storage solutions promptly to minimize losses on warehouse relocation; • Before typhoon season begins, temporarily reinforce warehouse doors, windows, and roofs to reduce the damaging effects of typhoons on warehouses.

• Improve the quality of construction materials, and change to high-quality equipment to reduce or avoid the impact of wind gusts; • In the future, when planning new warehouses, a new warehouse structure with typhoon-resistant and waterproof designs will be adopted to enhance resilience to extreme weather events.

• Elevate or implement waterproofing modifications for core facilities such as production workshops, storage warehouses, and cold storage units within plants to prevent seawater intrusion, and enhance plants' drainage systems with anti-corrosion measures to protect equipment from seawater damage; • Establish a storm surge early warning mechanism to send out early warning information in advance, clearly define evacuation routes, material relocation paths, and shelter points, and enhance emergency response and disaster resilience.

• Promote the optimization of the energy structure, reduce greenhouse gas emissions during the production process, and mitigate sea level rise caused by global warming; • Promote low-carbon production technologies and the application of green energy to enhance the Group's sustainable development capabilities.

• Fully implement fire patrol and inspection regulations to promptly identify and address fire hazards; • Organize regular fire safety training sessions and fire drills annually to enhance employees' fire safety awareness and improve their emergency response capabilities.

• Prior to the construction or expansion of factories, warehouses, or other facilities, make an all-around geographical risk assessment, and consider historical fire data, vegetation types, and wind speed, among others, to ensure selected sites are located away from fire-prone areas or high fire-risk areas.
• Regularly assess environment- and climate- related legal risks to ensure that corporate operations comply with national policies.

• Understand and actively participate in the carbon emissions trading market. If subsequently included in carbon quota control, effectively manage and optimize the Group's cost structure and risk exposure through strategic buying or selling of carbon quotas.

table_cells.text: ESG Aspects, General Disclosure and KPIs
Part B: Mandatory Disclosure Requirements This part sets out disclosure requirements that must be included in an issuer' s ESG report on a mandatory basis.

A statement from the board containing the following elements: (i) a disclosure of the board's oversight of ESG issues; (ii) the board's ESG management approach and strategy, including the process used to evaluate, prioritise and manage material ESG-related issues (including risks to the issuer's businesses); and (iii) how the board reviews progress made against ESG-related goals and targets with an explanation of how they relate to the issuer's businesses.

A description of, or an explanation on, the application of the following Reporting Principles in the preparation of the ESG report: Quantitative: Information on the standards, methodologies, assumptions and/or calculation tools used, and source of conversion factors used, for the reporting of emissions/energy consumption (where applicable) should be disclosed.

Materiality: The ESG report should disclose: (i) the process to identify and the criteria for the selection of material ESG factors; (ii) if a stakeholder engagement is conducted, a description of significant stakeholders identified, and the process and results of the issuer's stakeholder engagement.
Consistency: The issuer should disclose in the ESG report any changes to the methods or KPIs used, or any other relevant factors affecting a meaningful comparison.

A narrative explaining the reporting boundaries of the ESG report and describing the process used to identify which entities or operations are included in the ESG report. If there is a change in the scope, the issuer should explain the difference and reason for the change.
